pr_title: Raise error on unpermitted open redirects.
pr_body:
### Summary

Closes https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/39643

Trying https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/34412 again, this time with `redirect_back_or_to` support and a new framework default to opt into the new safer behaviour for redirection.

issue_context.title: Make redirect_to default to secure behavior to avoid open redirects
issue_context.body:
There is a known security issue with Rails `redirect_back`. Although there is a flag to fix the problem, by default, Rails allows for [open redirect attacks](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Unvalidated_Redirects_and_Forwards_Cheat_Sheet.html) as identified by OWASP in [CWE-601](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/601.html).

Here's an example exploit. An attacker modifies the Referrer header to point to a malicious website that looks like your app's login page. The user thinks they've been logged out so they enter their login credentials again, thereby giving their password to the attacker. The malicious website then redirects them back to the real application, and the user is none the wiser. If the application uses OAuth, the attacker will also receive the OAuth code which gives them access to the user's Google or Facebook account (with whatever permissions your app was granted).

Concerns about this were [raised back in 2018 as an RFC](https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/33577) which suggested the addition of an `allow_other_host` flag which defaults to `false`. Rails created the flag, but to maintain backward compatibility, they used the insecure default `true`. This ticket proposes that the default be changed to the secure default in the next major release.

It's important that Rails signal its intention to adopt the secure default because other projects are deferring to Rails on this issue. There is an [open ticket on ActiveAdmin](https://github.com/activeadmin/activeadmin/issues/6307) to adopt the secure default, but [the maintainers say they will not merge the PR until Rails signals that they will also adopt the secure default](https://github.com/activeadmin/activeadmin/pull/6308#issuecomment-644675396).

Importantly, ActiveAdmin and projects like it do not expose a flag which allows users to adopt the secure behavior. This makes it all the more important that Rails signal its intention to move to secure defaults.

Will the rails maintainers agree to using the secure default in the next major version upgrade?
comments: The allow_other_host change got reverted. There is an open issue for an alternative approach using strong parameters: #35019

@p8 `allow_other_host` appears to still be part of the codebase, here's the relevant github link:

https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/be3d9daaa39aa69603af16b602fe62ae47548469/actionpack/lib/action_controller/metal/redirecting.rb#L67-L94

I don't think the alternative approach with strong parameters will not apply to `redirect_back`.

The code shows that the method uses the insecure default: `allow_other_host` defaults to true. Can we make this default to false in the next major upgrade?

I think there are legitimate use cases for using `redirect_to` to external hosts, but in the cases of `redirect_back`, I would say the default should be `allow_other_host: false`. The original introduction of `allow_other_host` for `redirect_back` is https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/30850, and the current default was set just for backwards compatibility.
@p8 does that mean that the default for `redirect_back` will change in the next major rails upgrade?

👋 @williamcodes Sorry for the wait. This sounds like the same thing I tried to fix in https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/34412. We did fix it, and then had to revert it because it was too breaking of a change for some apps. I reverted it (https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/35018) and then opened an issue about the problem (https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/35019) that I haven't worked on since.

In the issue, I mention we want to shift to permitting external URLs with strong parameters. The bottom line is that I believe we are open to changing `redirect_to`'s behaviour, but not if it breaks legitimate redirects for legacy Rails apps. I've unassigned myself from the issue and closed it for now to stop gatekeeping any work.

Regarding `redirect_back` / `redirect_back_or_to`'s defaults, I'm not sure. It seems feasible to log a deprecation warning and then change it in the next version, but I'll get back to you on that. As @deivid-rodriguez points out, the original setting seems to be related to compatibility, and that's a good reason to change it.
@gmcgibbon I think we can change the defaults if we introduce a config and make new apps use a more secure default. Do you want to take a look?

Aha, that sounds like a good plan. Thanks @rafaelfranca! @tegon mentioned in the other issue that he wanted to pick this up. If he still wants to, I'd be happy to support him through it. Otherwise, I can start working on it.
@gmcgibbon I don't think I'll be able to work on this anytime soon. Feel free to grab it.
I could do it. I was looking for someone to help support me through it last year.

In that case:

You'll want to start by coding a config option in `actionpack` like `allow_open_redirects` or similar (eg. a `mattr_accessor` on `ActionController::Base`) that defaults to the current value (`true`).
Then, you'll want to make a `railties` config option ( eg. `action_controller.allow_open_redirects`) that sets the config value you created previously (`ActionController.allow_open_redirects`) in [an initializer in the action controller railtie](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/11e0c1092f2303f7dd35700565a114e649cf9145/actionpack/lib/action_controller/railtie.rb#L75).
Finally, you need to create a [Rails 6.2 new framework default](https://github.com/gmcgibbon/rails/blob/03516a924e71db7e065c8fb31c1d37af9b7c34ce/railties/lib/rails/generators/rails/app/templates/config/initializers/new_framework_defaults_6_2.rb.tt) that changes the value for new and upgrading apps (look at this PR for an example: https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/34692).

With the config option in place and the wiring in railties done, you simply need to replace the default with the config option in the redirecting module. There might be some extra legwork to do if this is only supported by `redirect_back` right now, we would want both `redirect_back` and `redirect_to` to respect the config value.

Let me know if that makes sense.
I like that `allow_open_redirects` config name 👍 We need to support it in `redirect_back_or_to` too (which `redirect_back` essentially delegates to).
@williamcodes are you still interested in working on this issue?

review_comments:

I think this is done. Take another look when you have time.

Perhaps we should name these variables more differently to make it more obvious how `_allow_other_host` is different from `allow_other_host`. Here's an alternative that reads a little clearer to me.

```suggestion
      allow_other_host = false if other_hosts_forbidden
```

Okay, good point. How about this?

```suggestion
      response_options.delete(:allow_other_host) if other_hosts_forbidden
```

If other hosts are forbidden, perhaps we should get the configuration out of params entirely, lest someone try to use it later on.

The difficulty here is mostly that we can't break existing behaviour for Rails apps that depend on it. Previously in #35018 I took a more extreme approach with no opt-in and it had to be reverted because it blocked upgrades. We need to add open redirect protection, but optionally turn it on when the opt-in is activated. We can make the behaviour default once we've given apps enough time to upgrade.

Right, yes, same page. In my mind, `other_hosts_forbidden` is checking to see if the configuration has been explicitly set to disallow other hosts. Another way of writing the same thing would be this:
```ruby
response_options.delete(:allow_other_host) if _allow_other_host == false
```

I think I'm missing the point of having a private `_redirect_to`. Right now you could call public `redirect_to` and it would make no difference. I tried for awhile to extract URL computation but I couldn't find a good way of doing it that didn't require multiple computations / perf regressions. 🙄 

I imagine if I get it right I will not need this line.

Here's another place I think we'd benefit from having a more explicit name for what _allow_other_host does. I flipped it from positive to negative, but you could do `other_hosts_permitted` instead if you wanted.

```suggestion
      response_options[:allow_other_host] ||= false if other_hosts_forbidden
```
`response_options[:allow_other_host] ||= false` would be a no-op if it is unset, `nil` and `false` are both falsy values.
This method feels too complex. Let's see if the other changes allow for slimming here otherwise I'll check back and suggest something on the next pass.
I moved the `raise` to a separate method, but feel free to make further suggestions 😄
